History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
31-year-old man with a 4-day history of intensely pruritic, red, sore, dry, cracked rash on chest, hands, and inner elbows, most consistent with an atopic dermatitis flare; treated with prior OTC steroid and antihistamines without relief.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Severe itch and erythematous rash disturbing sleep and concentration at work.  
• Onset/duration: Began 4 days ago; persisting and worsening; nightly showers give only brief relief.  
• Location: Chest, dorsal/volar hands, inner elbows; no facial, leg, or back involvement reported.  
• Character/progression: Very itchy, sore, dry, “cracked” skin; no vesicles, pus, bleeding, or systemic symptoms.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: Showers provide transient relief; OTC steroid cream and antihistamines tried without benefit.  
• ROS: Denies fever, cough, dyspnea, GI or urinary changes; no bleeding or discharge from lesions.

Past Medical History:
• Atopic dermatitis (eczema) – previous limited flares on arms.  
• Asthma – remote history, currently asymptomatic.  
• No other chronic illnesses noted.

Medications:
• OTC topical steroid cream – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• OTC oral antihistamines – name/dose/frequency not documented.  
• No regular prescriptions.
Allergies:
• Denies drug, food, or environmental allergies.

Social History:
• Lives with several flat-mates.  
• Occupation: Project manager at a pharmaceutical company.  
• Tobacco: Never smoker.  
• Alcohol: “A few beers per week.”  
• Recreation: Enjoys hiking but currently limited by rash.

Family History:
• Not discussed in transcript.

Physical Examination:
Vitals: Not recorded.  
Skin (video observation per clinician): Erythematous, dry, cracked patches on chest, hands, flexural elbows; appears consistent with eczema flare.  
Other systems: Not examined/documented.

Investigations:
• None ordered at this visit.

Assessment & Plan:
Overall Impression:
Likely acute flare of atopic dermatitis; consider allergic/irritant contact dermatitis or scabies if no improvement.

DDx Integration (brief):
1. Atopic dermatitis flare – strong past history, flexural involvement, dry/cracked skin, intense pruritus; no systemic signs.  
2. Allergic/irritant contact dermatitis – acute onset; chest/hands exposure; no identified trigger.  
3. Scabies – severe nocturnal itch and hand involvement, shared housing (support); no burrows or contact symptoms (oppose).

Issue 1 – Pruritic rash (probable eczema flare):
• Assessment: 4-day severe pruritic, erythematous, dry rash; likely atopic dermatitis.  
• Plan:
  – Prescribe stronger topical corticosteroid (specific agent not captured in transcript) for affected areas bid x7-10 days.  
  – Prescribe emollient for bath/shower and regular skin hydration.  
  – Prescribe oral Fexofenadine (dose/frequency not documented) for pruritus.  
  – Advise patient to keep diary of potential triggers (detergents, clothing, soaps).  
  – Educate on proper steroid use and moisturization techniques.  
  – Safety-net: Return in 1 week if no improvement or sooner if worsening, spreading, or systemic symptoms develop.

Issue 2 – Rule-out contact dermatitis / scabies if not improving:
• Assessment: Alternative etiologies remain possible given acute onset and communal living.  
• Plan:
  – Re-evaluate in follow-up; consider skin scraping for mites or referral to dermatology if persistent.  
  – Counsel patient to monitor flat-mates for similar symptoms.

Issue 3 – Health maintenance / lifestyle:
• Assessment: Generally healthy young adult.  
• Plan:
  – Encourage continued avoidance of smoking and responsible alcohol use.  
  – Support resumption of physical activities (hiking) once rash controlled.

General plan items:
• Provide written/online educational materials on eczema care.  
• Arrange follow-up appointment in 1 week or sooner if needed.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: No vitals, detailed skin description, or family history documented.  
● Conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: Audio intermittently unclear but key clinical data captured; no lab values provided.
